parts.name: LiPo battery 4S 5200 mAh
parts.blurb: A rechargeable lithium-polymer battery pack: 4 cells in series, 14.8 V, lots of capacity.
parts.used_for: Main power source for medium ground robots.
parts.notes: Never discharge below about 3.0 V per cell; charge with a balance charger, never unattended. (General guidance.)

parts.name: LiPo battery 4S 1500 mAh (5-inch quad)
parts.blurb: A smaller 4-cell LiPo pack sized for a 5-inch quadcopter.
parts.used_for: Flight battery for small quads where weight matters.
parts.notes: Flight packs work hard: retire a pack that comes down puffy or hot. (General guidance.)

parts.name: LiPo battery 3S 2200 mAh
parts.blurb: A 3-cell LiPo pack, 11.1 V — the classic small-robot battery.
parts.used_for: Main power for small rovers, RC cars and servo robots.
parts.notes: Never discharge below about 3.0 V per cell; balance-charge only. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Buck converter 5 V / 5 A
parts.blurb: Steps a higher battery voltage down to a clean 5 V.
parts.used_for: Powers the computer and logic from the main battery.
parts.notes: Budget its current for the hungriest load — an SBC under load plus servos can brown out a weak converter. (General guidance.)

parts.name: LiPo balance charger
parts.blurb: Charger that keeps every cell in a LiPo pack at the same voltage.
parts.used_for: Safely recharging LiPo packs between runs.
parts.notes: A balance charger is not optional for LiPo packs — it is how you avoid damaging cells. (General guidance.)

parts.name: XT60 pigtail lead
parts.blurb: A short lead with the yellow XT60 battery connector already soldered on.
parts.used_for: Connects the battery to the robot's power wiring.
parts.notes: XT60 is polarised, but check polarity before first plug-in — reversed power destroys electronics instantly. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Silicone wire 14 AWG (per metre)
parts.blurb: Flexible silicone-insulated wire thick enough for battery current.
parts.used_for: Main power runs between battery, fuse and drivers.
parts.notes: Match wire gauge to current: thin wire on a battery lead is a fuse you did not choose. (General guidance.)

parts.name: TB6612FNG dual motor driver
parts.blurb: A small dual motor driver: runs two DC motors forward, reverse and brake from logic signals.
parts.used_for: Driving the two (or four, with two boards) gearmotors of a small rover.
parts.notes: Rated about 1.2 A per channel continuous — right for small gearmotors, too small for big motors at stall. (General guidance.)

current_a_per_channel.quote: Output current maximum: 3 A per channel

parts.name: L298N dual motor driver module
parts.blurb: The classic red dual H-bridge module for two DC motors or one stepper.
parts.used_for: Cheap motor driving for school and hobby robots (it is the driver in the official Andino build).
parts.notes: It drops roughly 2 V across the bridge and runs hot, so motors see noticeably less than the battery voltage. (General guidance.)

parts.name: 4-in-1 ESC 45 A (BLHeli_S class)
parts.blurb: Four brushless speed controllers on one board for a quadcopter.
parts.used_for: Driving a quad's four brushless motors from the flight controller.
parts.notes: Match ESC current rating and cell count to motors and battery. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Brushed ESC 60 A (QuicRun 1060 class)
parts.blurb: A single brushed speed controller for an RC car's main motor.
parts.used_for: Lets a receiver/computer throttle one brushed motor.
parts.notes: Set its battery-type jumper correctly (LiPo cutoff) before first run. (General guidance.)

parts.name: ESP32 development board
parts.blurb: A Wi-Fi/Bluetooth microcontroller board — the robot's reflexes.
parts.used_for: Real-time jobs: motor PWM, encoder counting, sensor polling.
parts.notes: GPIO is 3.3 V logic and not 5 V tolerant — level-shift 5 V sensor outputs. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Teensy 4.1
parts.blurb: A very fast microcontroller board popular for precise motion control.
parts.used_for: Arms and robots that need many fast, timed control loops.
parts.notes: 3.3 V logic, not 5 V tolerant. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Raspberry Pi Pico (RP2040)
parts.blurb: Raspberry Pi's cheap dual-core microcontroller board.
parts.used_for: Small control jobs, custom sensor hubs, PIO-based timing tricks.
parts.notes: 3.3 V logic, not 5 V tolerant. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Raspberry Pi 5
parts.blurb: A full Linux computer the size of a credit card.
parts.used_for: The robot's brain: ROS 2, cameras, mapping, decision-making.
parts.notes: Needs a stiff 5 V / 5 A USB-C supply; undervoltage shows up as throttling and random reboots. (General guidance.)

parts.name: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano
parts.source: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Series Data Sheet (DS-11105-001)

specs.ai_performance: up to 67 TOPS (8 GB, Super mode)

parts.blurb: A GPU computer module for robots that see: camera AI on a board the size of a laptop memory stick.
parts.used_for: The robot's AI brain: vision models, perception and decision-making, with a GPU a Pi does not have.
parts.notes: Module only — it needs a carrier board, and its 5 V input must be sized for the 25 W top power mode; a sagging supply shows up as shutdowns under load. (Per the NVIDIA data sheet.)

parts.name: microSD card 128 GB (A2/V30)
parts.blurb: The removable flash card a Raspberry Pi boots from.
parts.used_for: Operating system, code and logged data storage.
parts.notes: The card is the robot's hard drive — a spare imaged card is cheap insurance. (General guidance.)

parts.name: SiK telemetry radio pair (915 MHz)
parts.source: Holybro SiK Telemetry Radio V3 class
parts.blurb: A pair of long-range radio modems that make a wireless serial link.
parts.used_for: Telemetry and parameter tuning for drones/field robots at range.
parts.notes: The 915 MHz variant suits the Americas; other regions use 433/868 MHz variants. (General guidance.)

parts.name: ExpressLRS receiver
parts.blurb: A tiny ExpressLRS radio-control receiver.
parts.used_for: Manual RC control link for cars, quads and boats.
parts.notes: Receiver and transmitter must run compatible ELRS versions and the same binding phrase. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Intel RealSense D435 depth camera
parts.blurb: A stereo depth camera: sees colour plus distance per pixel.
parts.used_for: Obstacle avoidance, 3D mapping, grasping.
parts.notes: Needs USB 3 for full depth rates; depth is unreliable in bright sunlight and on glass. (General guidance.)

photo.note: SLAMTEC publishes renders, not photographs, of the A1 — labelled a render wherever it appears.

parts.name: RPLIDAR A1 2D lidar
parts.blurb: A spinning 2D laser scanner — it sweeps a room and reports distances all around.
parts.used_for: Mapping and localisation for indoor rovers (SLAM). It is the lidar on Andino and the TurtleBot3 class.
parts.notes: Keep its scan plane unobstructed for the full 360 degrees or the map gets blind spots. (General guidance.)

parts.name: BNO055 9-DOF IMU breakout
parts.blurb: A 9-axis motion sensor with on-chip orientation fusion (compass + gyro + accelerometer).
parts.used_for: Heading and tilt sensing for rovers, humanoids and arms. Also the IMU in the official Andino BOM.
parts.notes: Keep it away from motors and power wires — magnetic interference corrupts its heading. (General guidance.)

parts.name: HC-SR04 ultrasonic ranger
parts.blurb: The two-eyed sonar module: pings and times the echo to measure distance.
parts.used_for: Cheap short-range obstacle detection on a budget.
parts.notes: Its echo pin outputs 5 V — divide it down before a 3.3 V input. Soft or angled surfaces absorb/deflect the ping. (General guidance.)

parts.name: PLA filament 1.75 mm, 1 kg
parts.blurb: The standard easy-print 3D printing plastic, on a 1 kg spool.
parts.used_for: Chassis plates, brackets and mounts (like this catalogue's CAD-kit parts).
parts.notes: PLA is stiff and easy but softens in a hot car; PETG is the tougher choice for parts near motors. (General guidance.)

parts.name: PETG filament 1.75 mm, 1 kg
parts.blurb: A tougher, slightly flexible printing filament.
parts.used_for: Functional brackets and parts that take knocks.
parts.notes: Prints hotter than PLA and strings more; a dried spool prints noticeably better. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Inline blade fuse holder + fuse
parts.blurb: A fuse holder wired into the battery's main lead.
parts.used_for: The last line of defence against a short circuit cooking the wiring.
parts.notes: Size the fuse above normal draw and below the wire's rating. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Emergency stop button (latching)
parts.blurb: A big latching red button that cuts power when slapped.
parts.used_for: Emergency stop for arms, humanoids and anything that can pinch.
parts.notes: Wire it in the main power path, not in software — it must work when the code doesn't. (General guidance.)

parts.name: BMS protection board 4S 40 A
parts.blurb: A battery-management board that protects a 4-cell pack from over/under-voltage.
parts.used_for: Protection for DIY 4S packs built from bare cells.
parts.notes: A BMS protects the pack; it is not a charger — still use a proper balance charger. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Custom PCB (KiCad import)
parts.source: imported from the builder's own KiCad project
parts.blurb: Your own circuit board, designed in KiCad and fabricated to order.
parts.used_for: Tidying a proven breadboard design into one reliable board.
parts.notes: Prove the circuit on a breadboard first — a PCB faithfully reproduces design mistakes. (General guidance.)

photo.note: Class exemplar: a Pololu 37D x54L mm 12 V gearmotor — the catalogue records the generic 37 mm class.

parts.name: DC gearmotor 12 V (37 mm class)
parts.blurb: A DC motor with a built-in gearbox: slow, strong turning for wheels.
parts.used_for: Driving rover wheels — torque matters more than speed here.
parts.notes: Stall current is several times the running current — size the driver for stall or limit current. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Brushed motor 540 size
parts.blurb: The standard 540-size brushed motor from RC cars.
parts.used_for: Main drive motor in 1/10 RC cars.
parts.notes: Brushed motors spark and wear brushes; gearing decides whether it is fast or strong. (General guidance.)

parts.name: MG996R servo
parts.blurb: A metal-gear hobby servo that turns to a commanded angle.
parts.used_for: Steering, grippers, camera tilts, small arm joints.
parts.notes: Power servos from their own regulated rail, not a microcontroller pin — brownouts reset controllers. (General guidance.)

photo.note: Waveshare's ST3215 listing — the Feetech STS3215 serial bus servo.

parts.name: STS3215 serial bus servo (Feetech)
parts.blurb: A serial-bus servo: many chain on one wire and report their position back.
parts.used_for: Humanoid, quadruped and arm joints that need feedback.
parts.notes: Each bus servo needs a unique ID set before chaining; the bus is half-duplex UART. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Stepper motor NEMA 17
parts.blurb: A stepper motor that moves in precise 1.8-degree steps.
parts.used_for: 3D printers, CNC axes, precise positioners.
parts.notes: Needs a stepper driver (A4988/DRV8825 class) — never wire coils straight to a microcontroller. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Brushless motor 2207 1960 KV
parts.blurb: An FPV quad motor: small, light, spins very fast.
parts.used_for: One of four motors on a 5-inch quadcopter.
parts.notes: KV times battery volts is roughly unloaded RPM — match prop size to KV and cell count. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Wheel 100 mm diameter
parts.source: generic 100 mm robot wheel (pathfinder demo spec)
parts.blurb: A 100 mm robot wheel — the size on the Pathfinder spec.
parts.used_for: Main drive wheels for medium rovers.
parts.notes: Wheel diameter sets both ground clearance and the distance each motor turn travels — the motion gate measures exactly this. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Mecanum wheel 100 mm

specs.note: mecanum odometry is unreliable by design; gate heading checks differ

parts.blurb: A wheel with angled rollers that lets a robot slide sideways.
parts.used_for: Holonomic (any-direction) drive on flat floors.
parts.notes: Mecanum rollers make wheel odometry unreliable by design — expect heading drift and fuse with an IMU. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Ball caster
parts.blurb: A free-rolling ball that supports the end of a two-wheel robot without steering it.
parts.used_for: The third contact point on differential-drive robots like Andino and TurtleBot3.
parts.notes: Casters carry weight but no drive — the robot's balance point should sit close to the driven axle. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Propeller 5x4.0x3 tri-blade
parts.blurb: A 5-inch tri-blade propeller for FPV quads.
parts.used_for: Thrust for 5-inch quadcopters.
parts.notes: Props are the dangerous part of a quad — remove them for every bench test. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Flight controller stack F405
parts.blurb: Flight-controller board stack that stabilises a quadcopter.
parts.used_for: Reads the gyro, runs the control loop, drives the ESCs.
parts.notes: Mount it soft (vibration isolation) — a rigidly mounted gyro reads the frame's buzz as motion. (General guidance.)

parts.name: 2-finger parallel gripper kit
parts.blurb: A two-finger parallel gripper kit (servo not included).
parts.used_for: The hand on a robot arm.
parts.notes: Check servo torque against gripper + payload weight at full reach, not just at the base. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Quadcopter frame 5 inch (carbon)
parts.blurb: A carbon-fibre frame sized for 5-inch propellers.
parts.used_for: The skeleton of a freestyle quadcopter.
parts.notes: Carbon fibre is conductive — insulate every board and wire that touches the frame. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Aluminium extrusion 2020 (per metre)
parts.blurb: Slotted aluminium profile, 20 by 20 mm, sold by the metre.
parts.used_for: Frames for arms, gantries and test rigs.
parts.notes: Uses M3/M4 T-slot nuts — order fasteners when you order lengths. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Chassis plate (3D-printed)
parts.blurb: The flat deck everything bolts onto — in RobotForge it is generated for your robot, ready to print.
parts.used_for: The base layer of a ground robot: motors, battery and boards all mount to it.
parts.notes: Keep mounting holes a few millimetres from plate edges in printed plastic, and print flat-side down. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Motor mount bracket (3D-printed)
parts.blurb: A small bracket that holds a gearmotor at exactly axle height.
parts.used_for: Bolting drive motors to the chassis plate.
parts.notes: Printed mounts flex under hard stall torque — gussets or a second bolt point help. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Lidar mount post (3D-printed)
parts.blurb: A post that raises the 2D lidar above the deck for a clear 360-degree view.
parts.used_for: Mounting a spinning lidar on rovers.
parts.notes: The lidar must see over the robot's own body in every direction, or the map has a permanent blind wedge. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Camera bracket (3D-printed)
parts.blurb: A small flat bracket that holds a camera facing forward.
parts.used_for: Mounting RGB/depth cameras on the chassis.
parts.notes: A slightly downward tilt sees near-field obstacles; level sees the horizon. Pick per job. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Ultrasonic bracket (3D-printed)
parts.blurb: A twin-can bracket sized for an HC-SR04-style ultrasonic ranger.
parts.used_for: Holding an ultrasonic sensor square to the direction of travel.
parts.notes: Angle it straight ahead: a tilted sonar measures the floor, not the wall. (General guidance.)

parts.name: Raspberry Pi Camera Module V2 (8 MP)
parts.source: Raspberry Pi Camera Module V2 (the camera in the official Andino BOM)
parts.blurb: The little ribbon-cable camera made for the Raspberry Pi.
parts.used_for: Vision on Pi-based robots — it is Andino's camera.
parts.notes: The CSI ribbon is fragile and keyed — seat it straight and never hot-swap it. (General guidance.)

parts.name: 18650 Li-ion pack 3S (3 cells)
parts.source: generic 18650 cells in a 3-cell holder (the battery in the official Andino BOM)
parts.blurb: Three cylindrical 18650 cells in series — 11.1 V of robot power.
parts.used_for: Main battery for small rovers — Andino runs on exactly this.
parts.notes: Use matched cells from one batch, and a holder with a fuse or BMS for a robot that drives unattended. (General guidance.)
